latest_release.name: Meteor 3.6.1
latest_release.body:
## v3.6.1, 2026-11-12

### Highlights

- Update Node.js to 26.13.1, preserving this release line’s Node major, with the [November 11 security fixes](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/november-2026-security-releases).
- Harden archive extraction, including symlink containment, and update the dev bundle to tar-fs 2.1.5.
- Expire email verification tokens, restrict client-side OAuth configuration in production, and reject malformed DDP messages without stalling connections.
- Fall back to MongoDB polling for selectors that cannot be safely re-evaluated locally, and preserve top-level `__proto__` data in oplog conversion.
- Prevent credential leakage through the HMR server and remove deployment settings from the legacy deployment information URL.
- Update the Cordova webapp plugin to reject unsafe asset paths and update the HTTP query parser.
- Update the npm installer dependencies and protect its JavaScript extraction fallback against paths and links escaping the installation directory.
- Restrict automatic accounts-express credential forwarding to trusted origins.

#### Breaking Changes

No general API removals. Security restrictions on previously unsafe behavior are described in Migration Steps.

#### Internal API changes

N/A

#### Migration Steps

Please run the following command to update your project:

```bash
meteor update --release 3.6.1
```

- Email verification tokens now expire after three days. Configure `emailVerificationTokenExpirationInDays` or `emailVerificationTokenExpiration` through `Accounts.config` on the server when a different lifetime is required.
- Configure OAuth services on the server or through settings in production. Client calls to `configureLoginService` require explicit server opt-in with `allowClientServiceConfiguration`.
- Queries using selectors that cannot be safely matched locally may use polling; monitor query load after updating.
- Unsafe archive or Cordova asset paths are rejected. Keep assets and extraction links within their intended directories.
- For automatic authentication to a separate trusted API origin, configure `Meteor.settings.public.packages["accounts-express"].authFetchAllowedOrigins`. Explicit Authorization headers remain supported.

#### Bumped Meteor Packages

- accounts-base@3.4.1
- accounts-express@1.0.1
- accounts-password@3.3.3
- ddp-server@3.6.1
- minimongo@2.2.2
- mongo@2.6.1
- webapp@2.4.1
- meteor-tool@3.6.1

#### Bumped NPM Packages

- cordova-plugin-meteor-webapp@2.0.5
- qs@6.16.1
- tar-fs@2.1.5 (dev bundle)
- tar@7.5.23 (npm installer)
- tmp@0.2.7 (npm installer)
- rimraf@6.1.4 (npm installer)

#### Special thanks to

- [@Grubba27](https://github.com/Grubba27)
- [@italojs](https://github.com/italojs)

discussions.title: Solutions for a private Meteor package registry
Fallback to plain JSON if EJSON parse fails on an incoming DDP message
Feature request: native self-service email-change flow in `accounts-password`
`accounts-password` stores email-verification and password-reset tokens in plaintext (login tokens are hashed)
`meteor npm`/`meteor node` inside a built bundle should honor the bundle's release
RFC: An explicit lifecycle for server Sessions
Cooldown capability for the meteor node bundled npm version and Atmosphere packages
Should Meteor have an official router package maintained by the core team?

Meteor is an **ultra-simple** environment for building **modern** web applications.
- [Official Website](https://www.meteor.com) - [Installation](https://docs.meteor.com/about/install.html) - [Documentation](https://docs.meteor.com/#/full/)
### 📚 **Create your applications using modern JavaScript** Benefit from the latest technology updates to rapidly prototype and develop your applications.
### ✨ **Integrate technologies you already use** Use popular frameworks and tools right out-of-the-box. Focus on building features instead of configuring disparate components yourself.
### 💻 **Build apps for any device** Use the same code whether you’re developing for web, iOS, Android, or desktop for a seamless update experience for your users.

# 🧱 Developer Resources **Building an application with Meteor?** * Build with AI coding assistants using [Meteor Agent Skills](https://docs.meteor.com/ai/agent-skills) * Deploy on [Galaxy](https://galaxycloud.app) * Find packages on [Atmosphere](https://atmospherejs.com/) * Discuss on [Forums](https://forums.meteor.com/) * Join the [Meteor Discord](https://discord.gg/hZkTCaVjmT) If you’ve run into a bug, check the [issue tracker](https://github.com/meteor/meteor/issues). To propose a feature, [start a discussion](https://github.com/meteor/meteor/discussions/). # 🤝 Help with an upcoming release For the goals behind each release and what comes next, see the [Meteor roadmap](https://docs.meteor.com/about/roadmap.html). Start with an unassigned issue or an open pull request in a release milestone. When you [triage a bug report](https://github.com/meteor/meteor/blob/devel/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md#bugs), share the steps that reproduce it and the Meteor version you tested. For a regression, include the last version that worked. You can also help maintainers close an issue by linking the fix or the original report for a duplicate. For a superseded PR, link its replacement. The focus badges show related issues and PRs across milestones. To see how the labels work together, follow [an installer bug from report to release](https://github.com/meteor/meteor/blob/devel/LABELS.md#an-example-from-a-bug-report-to-its-release). If you find another fix that fits the release, share your test results on its issue or PR. The patch row links to open bugs in areas covered by the [Meteor 3.6 release notes](https://docs.meteor.com/history#v3-6-0-2026-11-10). Know one of the areas below? Try a PR in your app, tell the author what you found, and check back when a revision is ready.
